_: THE CHATGPT CONTRACT. Actuation is DOM (type, click send, set the file
input); the ANSWER is read off the network. Every value here was measured
on the live signed-in app on 2026-09-06 with `uibridge recon`, not
guessed - the guessed version of this file was never enabled.
The UI on this account is pt-BR. Nothing below matches on English button
text: data-testids and ids are what the app itself keys on.
_wire: answer  POST /backend-api/f/conversation streams text/event-stream in the
'v1' delta encoding (see transports/sse-openai.mjs). The page sends
it - with its sentinel tokens, which are never forged here - and
the tap reads the response the page receives. The body carries the
model's markdown, the slug of the model that answered, and its
sources with the offsets of every inline citation.
upload  MEASURED 2026-09-06 by setting input#upload-files with a PDF and
recording every request: POST /backend-api/files (gets a signed
upload_url) -> PUT the bytes to oaiusercontent.com -> POST
with event 'file.processing.file_ready'. That last call, one per
file, with file_ready in its body, is the readiness signal. (An
earlier guess of /files/<id>/uploaded never fired: the file sat
attached and the prompt was never sent.)
effort  the page's own request body carries the picker state: `model`
(gpt-5-6 at Instantânea, gpt-5-6-thinking at Média AND Alta) and
_composer: A ProseMirror editor. Its no-JS fallback, textarea[name=prompt-textarea], sits
EARLIER in the DOM and is hidden - listing it as an alternative made
.first() resolve to the hidden node and wait 30s for it to become visible.
_sendButton: aria-label 'Enviar prompt' on this account; the testid is language-neutral.
_response: Only a FALLBACK: the answer normally comes off the wire. Turns render as
[data-message-author-role] node; the copy control is 'Copiar mensagem'.

_ordinalNode: MEASURED 2026-09-09 by reloading a six-message thread and sampling the
DOM every 150ms. At 10.4s it mounted conversation-turn-2 .. -6 and NEVER
mounted turn 1 - not in 20s of sampling, and not after scrolling every
scrollable ancestor to the top. The thread had 123px of scroll overflow,
so reached_top and reached_bottom were both legitimately TRUE and the
export would have claimed complete while missing the user's opening
message. ChatGPT numbers every turn in data-testid; that number is the
only evidence that says whether the DOM ever showed the start of the
thread. Numbering is per MESSAGE, not per pair: 6 messages = turns 1-6.
_attachmentNode: MEASURED 2026-09-09 against a real turn carrying a CSV. The previous
selector was a DIRECT-CHILD div selector and matched nothing, so every
exported ChatGPT thread silently reported zero attachments on turns
that had them - an audit record that omits the annex it was sent.
the name lives in a SPAN: span.grow.items-center.truncate.font-semibold
.capitalize. Descendant, not child; span, not div. Scored on the live
page: 2 hits on user turns, 0 on assistant turns.
NOTE the label is the SITE'S rendered name - ChatGPT drops the
extension and title-cases it (probe_annex_123.csv -> Probe Annex 123),
which is why export labels do not match the uploaded filename.

_export: MEASURED 2026-09-06 on a live thread: every message renders as a node
carrying data-message-author-role and a STABLE data-message-id (a uuid),
and assistant nodes also carry data-message-model-slug. Those ids are what
makes de-duplication across a virtualized scroll trustworthy.
There is no history JSON to read instead: loading the native /c/<uuid> URL
sends POST /backend-api/f/conversation/prepare whose response is only
{status, conduit_token}; the messages arrive over the app's own runtime.
MEASURED 2026-09-06: a SENT file renders inside the message node itself
as a card whose name sits in div.overflow-hidden > div.truncate.font-semibold.
Note ChatGPT renames repeats server-side (_attach_probe(3).md), so the
exported name is what the THREAD shows, not what was on disk.

_models: family x effort, named the way the UI presents them (instant / medium /
high). A request is VERIFIED when the wire's model_slug matches `slug`
AND the request body's thinking_effort equals `sentEffort` (null = the
field is absent, which is what Instantânea sends).
VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-06 on the 5.6 family: instant -> gpt-5-6 with no
effort field (auto-routes: a PDF question at this setting was answered by
gpt-5-6-thinking, so the instant slug pattern admits it); medium ->
gpt-5-6-thinking + standard; high -> gpt-5-6-thinking + extended. The 5.5
family is the same shape by construction of the picker; see git log for
_fileInput: A hidden input[type=file] with no accept filter and `multiple`, so PDFs
and CSVs go straight in; the two testid'd inputs (upload-photos-input,
upload-media-input) are image/media only. No chip selector: readiness is
the upload confirmation on the wire.

_auth: MEASURED on 2026-09-06 against a live signed-out session:
anonAssetPattern  chatgpt.com serves the WHOLE anonymous app from
/unauth-mweb/ - a different bundle, a different
composer (textarea#mobile-composer-prompt), and file
inputs that accept image/* only. That is a fact about
the server's response rather than about page wording,
so it is the strongest negative signal available.
cookies seen      oai-did, oai-mweb-origin, oai-sc, g_state - device
and telemetry ids, no session token.
VERIFIED 2026-09-06 in BOTH directions:
signed in    /api/auth/session reported a configured account field;
only boolean presence leaves the page. The endpoint is
authoritative and the cookie pattern never has to
fire. NOTE its response also carries a bearer token and
says so itself, which is why core/auth.mjs does the field
lookup inside the page and keeps none of the payload.
signed out   `uibridge doctor chatgpt --anon`, on a throwaway profile
that has never logged in: verdict anonymous, proven by the
/unauth-mweb/ bundle.
authCookiePattern is VERIFIED as of 2026-09-06 against this live
signed-in profile. The session cookie is CHUNKED: the jar carries
__Secure-next-auth.session-token.0 (3933 chars) and .1 (200 chars),
and no unchunked __Secure-next-auth.session-token at all - so the
pattern is deliberately a PREFIX match, not an exact name. Cookie
NAMES and lengths were read; values never are.
It remains a positive-only signal: the verdict still falls through to
the endpoint and then to the anonymous-bundle test rather than
claiming a session that is not there.
WHY THIS MATTERS MORE HERE THAN ANYWHERE ELSE: chatgpt.com answers while
logged out. A request against a signed-out browser does not fail; it
succeeds with a weaker model and nothing marks the result.
challengeText: unusual activity|verify you are human|not a robot|Just a moment
_picker: MEASURED 2026-09-06. The composer pill (its text is the current effort,
'Instantânea' by default; on hover 'Esforço de raciocínio') opens ONE
popover with TWO panels, switched by data-active:
simple view    the EFFORT slider - aria-valuenow 0 Instantânea, 1 Média,
2 Alta, 3 Pro ('Upgrade necessário' on this plan; the
value refuses to move there). Its help text says to use
the arrow keys, so that is how it is driven.
advanced view  the FAMILY radios (menuitemradio): 'GPT-5.6 Sol' (checked
by default) and 'GPT-5.5'. Reached by clicking the row
labelled 'Selecionar modelo'; a click on a radio while the
simple view is up is intercepted by that panel.
One Escape steps back a panel; a second closes the popover. The header
has no model-switcher button on this build.
_previewPanel: MEASURED 2026-09-08 by diffing every data-testid in the page before and
after a real click on button.behavior-btn. The click opens an artifact
the generic [data-testid=stage-thread-flyout]; for a CSV the body is a
spreadsheet editor (a swarm of popcorn-* testids). Both are absent before
the click and present after, which is what makes them usable as evidence
A class-substring guess was tried first and refuted in the same run:
[class*=artifact] already matches something on a thread page before any
click, so it would have reported 'progressed' unconditionally.
_previewDownload: MEASURED 2026-09-09, and it settles a defect that had been open since
2026-09-08: `export --files` could not retrieve a file from a thread the
browser had merely RELOADED, while the same file came down perfectly at
the moment the answer arrived.
The two paths are genuinely different mechanisms, not one flaky one:
AT GENERATION TIME the app owns the bytes. Clicking button.behavior-btn
makes the PAGE fetch interpreter/download then estuary/content as an
ordinary in-page request, so the wire tap reads the response body and
Chrome writes no file. That is the `wire` source.
ON A RELOADED THREAD the same click issues NO REQUEST AT ALL. It opens
the artifact preview panel and stops there - measured three times, with
Network.requestWillBeSent and Browser.downloadWillBegin both armed:
zero app requests, zero downloads, panel present. Repeat clicking (the
old behaviour) can only toggle that panel, which is why the failure
read as '3 clicks produced no request - the page never asked for it'.
The panel's OWN toolbar holds the control that fetches. It is a bare
icon button, no data-testid, identified only by aria-label - 'Baixar'
on this pt-BR account. Clicking it produces:
GET /backend-api/estuary/content?id=file_..&fn=..&cd=attachment
and, because of that cd=attachment, A REAL BROWSER DOWNLOAD.
WHICH IS WHY THIS PATH DOES NOT USE THE WIRE TAP. Measured on the same
click: the tap SEES the request and then fails to read the body with
net::ERR_ABORTED - a download is not an in-page fetch, and there is no
response body for CDP to hand back. Chrome's own download event is the
only place the bytes exist, so this path captures those instead and
reports source 'browser'. Reading the panel is not a second-guess at the
wire path; it is the only transport that has the file.
previewDownload is a LABEL PATTERN, not a selector, because that button
has no stable structural identity: its only distinguishing marks are the
aria-label and an svg <use href=..sprites-core-<hash>.svg#be92c3>, and
the hash changes with every asset deploy. Its neighbour 'Tela cheia'
(fullscreen) carries the identical class list. Only the pt-BR spelling
was measured here; the others are the same kind of alternation `notices`
already uses, and a miss is reported honestly rather than guessed past.
_generatedFile: MEASURED 2026-09-06 on real code-interpreter turns, end to end.
ChatGPT does NOT put a file behind a viewer overlay the way Gemini does.
The answer text itself carries the link:
[Download trials.csv](sandbox:/mnt/data/trials.csv)
and the rendered link is <button class='behavior-btn'> whose aria-label is
the link text (no href, no <a download>, so scanning for download
affordances finds nothing). Clicking it makes the PAGE fetch:
GET /backend-api/conversation/<id>/interpreter/download
?message_id=..&sandbox_path=/mnt/data/trials.csv
-> {download_url, file_name, mime_type, metadata:{file_id}}
GET /backend-api/estuary/content?..  -> the bytes, with
content-disposition: attachment; filename="trials.csv"
WHY WE READ THE RESPONSE INSTEAD OF LETTING CHROME DOWNLOAD IT:
- Chrome writes NO FILE. Measured with Browser.setDownloadBehavior set to
allow + a download path: zero download events, empty directory. The app
fetches the bytes and keeps them in the page.
- Calling those endpoints ourselves is impossible without the app's bearer
token: an in-page fetch with cookies AND Playwright's request context
both return 401 'Unauthorized - Access token is missing'. Lifting the
user's token out of the session is not something this project does.
So the page clicks and we keep the bytes it received - byte-exact, so an
xlsx or a png survives, and named by the server rather than by a label.
THE CLICK IS THE HARD PART, and it cost four runs to see it:
- the rate-limit modal's backdrop swallows every click, and it REAPPEARS
every few seconds while the lock is active (each conversations poll
returns 429 and re-raises it), so it must be dismissed immediately
before the click, not once per request;
- the app's own layout panels (data-side-pane-shell-host, the sticky
composer) cover a link at the bottom of a thread, so Playwright reports
'subtree intercepts pointer events' - the element is centred first and,
if still covered, the click is dispatched on the element itself;
- a click can be ACCEPTED AND IGNORED during the re-render after a modal
closes, so success is judged by the page actually issuing the request,
and the click is repeated until it does.
VERIFIED: 74 bytes of real CSV on disk with the right header and rows.
SCOPE: downloadable files linked through the code-interpreter /mnt/data
path, regardless of extension or MIME type. UI-native Canvas/textdoc
objects are deliberately outside the file-transfer contract.

notices.name: rate limit
notices.match: Excesso de solicitações|solicitações rápido demais|Limitamos temporariamente|too many requests|Rate limit

_notices: MEASURED 2026-09-06, and it cost two failed download runs before it was
looked at properly. After a burst of requests the site raises a MODAL:
body   'Você está fazendo solicitações rápido demais. Limitamos
temporariamente o acesso às suas conversas para proteger seus
dados. Aguarde alguns minutos antes de tentar novamente'
markup role=dialog inside a 'fixed inset-0 z-50' backdrop
It is a per-user data-protection lock, NOT a bot challenge: new chats
still send and answer, only previous conversations are blocked. But the
backdrop covers the page, so EVERY click is intercepted - Playwright
reports 'subtree intercepts pointer events' and a download click times out
with no request ever sent. So it is dismissed before actuation and reported
in the result; the pacer (minIntervalMs) is what keeps it from appearing.
_unhydratedComposer: MEASURED 2026-09-09. When the app fails to start, the page still shows a
no-JS fallback. It is NOT the composer - typing into it leaves
button[data-testid=send-button] disabled, because nothing is listening.
Its presence WITHOUT div#prompt-textarea[contenteditable] is therefore a
precise diagnosis: the application never mounted. Compare with the old
note under _composer, which recorded this same textarea as hidden and
excluded it from the composer selector for that reason; on this build it
is visible, which is why a bare selector wait reported nothing useful.
CAUSE: a launch race. With the browser window parked at -32000 (the
default 'offscreen' mode) Chrome sometimes composites no frame and the
editor, which mounts from a frame callback, never appears. Measured across
repeated launches: offscreen failed twice and succeeded once; a visible
launch mounted every time, and once mounted the app survives being parked,
reloaded and even minimised. See DomProvider.#recoverUnhydrated.
